lead_outcomes.reason: The AU call says: 'The EAN Fellowship is open to youth- and women-led small enterprises that are: registered and operating in an AU Member State; formally registered as a business entity; operating for at least two years; and employing a minimum of three full-time staff.' The profile records no registered business. The call also closed ('Application Deadline: 30 September 2026').

DAAD's scholarship-database entry for the Heilbronn AI Fellowships targets 'International PhD candidates or postdoctoral researchers who obtained a PhD/doctorate no more than five years ago' and says PhD candidates should be in the final year before their dissertation defence. The profile holds a Bachelor's degree only and is not enrolled in a doctorate. (Page answers HTTP 403 to the repo reader; read with WebFetch.)

The Philippine-American Educational Foundation (Fulbright Philippines) page says applicants 'must be citizens of one of the 10 ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste'. The Democratic Republic of the Congo is neither. (The Philippine deadline was October 16, 2026.)

The US-UK Fulbright Commission page says: 'To be eligible, students must: Be a US citizen and possess a US passport'. The applicant is a DRC citizen. (The programme is also for US undergraduates with at least two years of study remaining.)

UNICEF USA's own expression-of-interest form describes a 'Learning Exchange for Cities' within its work 'focused on supporting cities in establishing or strengthening Youth Councils', asks for the 'City/justisdiction you represent' and says 'we'll follow up by the end of December to let you know whether your city has been selected'. It is for local-government staff of (U.S.) cities; the profile holds no such role.

The organiser's page says: 'Applications for the GEAF Ambassador Programme 2027 have officially closed.' Later applications are kept for future iterations. GEAF is a Geneva-based, UNEP-accredited non-profit; no fee seen. Nationality rules were not shown on the page.

The AU Peace Fund call says 'the beneficiaries of the AU Peace Fund under the programmatic windows are: Member States of the African Union; Regional Economic Communities (RECs); Regional Mechanisms (RMs); and The Political Affairs, Peace and Security (PAPS) Department of the African Union Commission.' Individuals cannot apply. The window ran 'from 1st August to 15 September 2026'.

The organiser's terms of reference (CEFOREP SARL, 'Termes de référence des formations – Novembre à Décembre 2026', page 10, published as an image on the listing) state 'Frais de participation : 75 000 FCFA par participant' and 'Période et horaires : Du 04 au 10 novembre 2026', in CEFOREP's training rooms in N'Djamena, Chad. A paid, in-person commercial course that has already taken place; the text exists only in the image, so the quote must be read on the image.

FirstRand's own scholarship page says the partnership is 'to enable one outstanding South African student a year to undertake postgraduate study at the Blavatnik School of Government' and that FirstRand and the School want applicants who will 'contribute to South Africa on their return'. The applicant is a DRC citizen. (Applications 16 October 2026 to 25 February 2027. Page read in Chrome: WebFetch fails with a TLS certificate error and the repo reader gets no response.)
